description: Research a listed company against your investment strategy: business, moat, growth signals, management, risks and catalysts, with the off-consensus evidence that creates alpha.
suggested_questions: Do a fundamental deep dive on Duolingo (DUOL, duolingo.com) for a long/short fund testing a long thesis on paid subscriber growth and pricing power.
Do a fundamental deep dive on Celsius Holdings (CELH, celsius.com) for a growth fund deciding whether the Alani Nu acquisition strengthens its position in energy drinks.
Do a fundamental deep dive on Wolfspeed (WOLF, wolfspeed.com) for a value fund deciding whether the post-restructuring equity is investable.
skill:
How hedge funds underwrite a position:
- The thesis is a variant perception: what the price implies, what the fund expects instead, why that view is better
  informed, and which observable events would prove it right or wrong. Alpha comes from evidence the market has not
  priced, usually found outside the company's own summary of itself.
- The strategy in the request (long, short, growth, value, event-driven, a named theme) sets which evidence matters.

Where the evidence lives:
- Business and financials: 10-K, 10-Q, 20-F and 8-K filings on SEC EDGAR, earnings releases (8-K exhibit 99.1),
  investor day decks and the investor relations site. Segment notes and footnotes often hold what summaries leave out.
- Moat and competition: competitors' own filings and pricing pages, customer case studies, partner announcements,
  trade press, patent and trademark filings, app store and review pages, archived pages at web.archive.org.
- Off-consensus signals: careers pages and ATS boards (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday) for hiring by function and
  region, pricing and product pages over time, new subsidiaries in state and foreign registries, federal awards on
  USAspending, permits, recalls and complaints in regulator databases (FDA, NHTSA, CPSC, CFPB).
- Management: 8-K Item 5.02 for officer changes, Form 4 for insider trades, DEF 14A for pay and board, past guidance
  in earnings releases compared with reported results.
- Risks: risk factors and legal proceedings in filings, CourtListener and state court portals, SEC and DOJ releases,
  short-seller reports and the company's rebuttal.
- Catalysts: earnings dates and investor days on the IR site, FDA calendars, ClinicalTrials.gov, lockup terms in
  prospectuses, debt maturities in the debt footnote, shareholder meeting dates in proxies.

What terms mean:
- Consensus is what published sell-side previews, company guidance and financial press say the market expects. It is
  reported as published, never invented.
- A moat factor is durable only when evidence shows it holding over time (retention, pricing power, switching costs,
  scale, network effects, IP). High margins or retention alone are symptoms, not causes.
- reads_as on a signal is relative to the strategy in the request: supports, contradicts or neutral.

Pitfalls: company-promoted metrics without a definition, stale figures repeated by aggregators, a segment confused
with the whole company, and trailing figures presented as current.

Citations and evidence:
- source_url is one full public https URL: the exact page the value was read on. Never a search results page, an index
  page, an internal file path or a source id. A value from two pages is two values.
- Dates are the date the event happened or the source printed, as YYYY-MM-DD, not today's date.
- Public pages only. Paywalled, logged-in or leaked material, expert-network transcripts and anything marked
  confidential carry MNPI risk and are out of bounds. When only a paywalled article's headline and first lines are
  public, those lines can be used, marked "Headline only:".
- Evidence grades: primary_record (regulator, court, filing, government database, lender schedule, or the live or
  archived page being measured), company_statement, original_press, repeated_press, third_party_tracker. When a page
  repeats a filing, a release or another outlet, the original is the better citation.
- A value nobody published is null. Not an estimate from memory. Analyst opinions, estimates, price targets and
  ratings are views, not evidence.
- Entity drift is the most common error: a namesake, a parent, a subsidiary, a lender or a sister company. Match on
  legal name, ticker, SEC CIK or domain before using a page.

output_schema.description: Fundamental deep dive on one listed company.

legal_name.description: Legal name as on SEC filings.

as_of.description: Date of the latest evidence used, YYYY-MM-DD.

thesis_read.description: Three to five sentences on how the evidence reads against the strategy in the request: what supports it, what contradicts it, and the single most important open question. No price target or trade call.

business.description: What the company sells and how it makes money.

what_it_sells.description: Products or services and main customer types.

revenue_model.description: How revenue is earned (subscription, usage, unit sales, licensing...).

segments.description: Reported segments with their latest revenue as printed.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.

financials.description: Latest reported figures and the prior comparable period, as printed.

items.description: Latest reported figures and the prior comparable period, as printed.

period.description: Fiscal period, e.g. FY2025 or Q3 FY2026.

metric.description: Metric name as reported, e.g. revenue, operating income, free cash flow, net debt.

unit.description: Currency and scale, e.g. USD millions.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.

factor.description: Moat factor or competitive force, e.g. pricing power, switching costs, new entrant.

evidence.description: What the source shows, with figures where printed.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.

alpha_signals.description: Off-consensus observations from outside the company's own summary of results.

items.description: Off-consensus observations from outside the company's own summary of results.

observation.description: What was observed, with numbers and dates where printed.

reads_as.description: Direction relative to the strategy in the request.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.

management.description: Key executives and what the record shows about them.

items.description: Key executives and what the record shows about them.

since.description: Start date in role, YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY.

record.description: Delivery against past guidance, prior roles, insider buying or selling.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.

severity.description: high: could break the thesis; medium: could dent it; low: worth tracking.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.

catalysts.description: Dated events ahead that could move the stock.

items.description: Dated events ahead that could move the stock.

expected_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, or a period like 2026-Q4 when only that is published.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.

variant_view.description: Where the evidence departs from consensus.

consensus.description: What published previews, guidance or press say the market expects, as published.

evidence_against_consensus.description: Evidence found here that the consensus may be missing.

what_would_change_the_view.description: Observable developments that would confirm or break the thesis.

checked_no_finding.description: Searches that came back empty, so a gap is a verified absence rather than a skipped check.

items.description: Searches that came back empty, so a gap is a verified absence rather than a skipped check.

result.description: What came back, e.g. no filing found, register shows no case.
